title: Ordered insertion gives a local homotopy inverse
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $r\in\mathbb N$, $U:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to X.\mathrm{Opens}$ any family, and $G$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module. Let $\epsilon:G[0]\to C$ be the explicit increasing-tuple sheaf augmentation [def-pc-s3-alternating-cech-sheaf-construction]. For every $i:\operatorname{Fin}(r)$, restricting the extension by zero of $\epsilon$ from natural to integer degrees to $U_i$ is a homotopy equivalence of complexes of $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-modules. No covering condition and no pullback morphism are assumed.

source.place: Tag 02FU (local insertion contraction), adapted to increasing tuples using Tag 01FM (alternating comparison); parent local-contraction proof

proof.text: On a test open contained in U_i, define the inverse in degree zero by projection to the singleton i. In degree p+1, define h into degree p coordinatewise: insert i in the unique increasing position a of the target tuple, with sign (-1)^a, and take zero if the tuple already contains i. Adjoining i leaves the intersection with the test open unchanged, so identify the section modules along this equality rather than reversing a restriction map. These operators are linear and commute with restrictions. The reverse augmentation composite is the identity.

proof.text: Expand dh+hd coordinatewise. For a tuple without i, deletion of the inserted i contributes the identity. Pair all other deletions with insertion after deletion; their restriction composites agree and their signs are opposite. For a tuple already containing i, only deletion of i followed by reinsertion contributes, again with sign one. In degree zero the missing incoming term is augmentation followed by singleton projection. These identities give both inverse homotopies on presheaves over U_i. Additive sheafification and open restriction preserve them and identify sheafification of the original sheaf with itself. Extend the inverse and homotopies by zero to integer degrees using Mathlib Homotopy.extend, so the extended restricted augmentation is a homotopy equivalence.

theorem alternatingCechSheafAugmentation_restrict_homotopyEquivalence
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {r : ℕ} (U : Fin r → X.Opens) (G : X.Modules) (i : Fin r) :
    HomologicalComplex.homotopyEquivalences (U i).toScheme.Modules (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
      (((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (U i).ι).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map (HomologicalComplex.extendMap
          (alternatingCechSheafAugmentation U G) ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat))
